correspondence.component_scope: Selected headward opening and initial northward passage
correspondence.finding: Both originals expose the selected headward opening within the Inland Ice south of the exposed northern Greenland land belt. The regional sheet shows the same pale ice unit identified in its legend. The opening and its full northward continuation lie inside that sheet, rather than in the blank area outside its neatline. No river label or continuous mapped natural channel is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Initial short turns and transition into the westward ice-sheet corridor
correspondence.finding: The small northern turns and subsequent westward departure are completely within the ice-covered area on both maps. The original national blue linework is identified by its legend as ice surface contours and ice-thickness information, not a river network. Every selected short part and its geographic connection to the opening and western continuation was read.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward passage to and across the regional western edge
correspondence.finding: The westward selected corridor remains in mapped Inland Ice. The regional sheet covers the eastern passage and ends at its western meridian within the last part of this component. The national original visibly overlaps this edge and continues across the entire remaining corridor. The map edge is not a source-coverage gap; the regional sheet is not used as evidence beyond its actual extent.

correspondence.component_scope: Long westward middle sequence and its successive small bends
correspondence.finding: The national original covers every stored part of the long westward middle sequence, including successive northward and southward offsets and all intervening joins. The setting remains the northern Inland Ice south of the exposed-rock belt. No lake, wetland or managed-water connection is inferred from the ice contours, sub-ice contours or modeled line.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern approach, short southward return and final westward bend
correspondence.finding: The northwestern turn, brief return and westward continuation all lie in the same exposed national-map ice-sheet setting. Their junction with the last long northward part is covered. Geographic terrain correspondence is complete; surface or subglacial hydraulic continuity is not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Final long northward passage and actual selected endpoint in southern Freuchen Land
correspondence.finding: The final selected part is read northward from the Inland Ice, through the southern Freuchen Land exposed-rock and local-ice terrain, to its actual ending in the mapped ice-covered interior of southern Freuchen Land. The endpoint was inspected directly, rather than stopping at a nearby coast or adopting the neighboring J. P. Koch Fjord label. This historical cartography does not establish a conventional river mouth or substantiate the modeled sea-terminal classification. Exact current glacier or shoreline boundaries are not needed for this terrain-level conclusion.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southern opening and Pogopuk Creek mountain valley
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening lies on the mapped upper Pogopuk Creek channel. Repeated labels and the continuous northward mountain-valley channel cover the selected headward reach and its intervening side-feeder junctions. The selection locally cuts small bends but remains in this connected creek corridor. The chosen opening is not asserted to be the ultimate natural source or a formal name-boundary point.

correspondence.component_scope: Pogopuk Creek joining Kavik River
correspondence.finding: The upper original shows Pogopuk Creek entering the separately labelled Kavik River, which approaches from the east. The combined braided waterway continues north. The observed confluence supports the reach-name transition without assigning the receiving name to the upstream creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Kavik River northward foothill corridor
correspondence.finding: Repeated Kavik River labels and continuous channels cover the northward valley, smaller incoming streams, and the transition from foothills into wetland-bordered braided reaches. Lakes beside the corridor are lateral features; no selected through-lake or glacial passage is required.

correspondence.component_scope: Kavik River northwest turn and braided plain
correspondence.finding: The original maps show Kavik River turning northwest through the airstrip vicinity and a broad branching alluvial corridor, then turning north. Multiple mapped channels and their joins establish the ordinary through-corridor. The selected straight segments locally cut across bars, the floodplain and bends, including north of the broad main braid. The finding concerns the connected Kavik corridor rather than a separate present channel along every modeled segment. This middle turn is not the downstream Shaviovik confluence.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Kavik River across the wetland and lake-rich coastal plain
correspondence.finding: The lower original repeatedly labels Kavik River along its continuous northward braided and meandering channel. Surrounding ponds and wetland areas do not replace the mapped river connection. All selected intervening joins and the eastern and western bend excursions remain within this ordinary river corridor; the source does not require a through-lake, impoundment or managed connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Kavik–Shaviovik confluence
correspondence.finding: Near the delta, the separately labelled Shaviovik River approaches from the west and joins the northward Kavik corridor. The combined downstream braided channel is labelled Shaviovik River. This lower mapped junction, not the earlier northwest bend, supports the representative receiving-river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Shaviovik delta and actual Mikkelsen Bay terminal
correspondence.finding: The terminal original shows the named Shaviovik River continuing through its connected braided delta to Mikkelsen Bay. The actual selected endpoint is in the eastern distributary-mouth setting. Enlarged source reading covers the final western bend, cross-delta generalized segments, eastern branch and coastal outlet; connecting delta channels are visible. Correspondence is established at ordinary delta scale without selecting a current active distributary, an exact bank, or a formal river-to-bay boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern selected opening and first northwestward feeder
correspondence.finding: The initial eastern feeder and its successive northwestward bends match the depicted drainage. Its local name is unestablished; the Magda label is not extended to this opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper middle west-northwestward corridor and joins
correspondence.finding: Figure 6b shows the connected drainage through this corridor. Figure 2’s green glacial-lake reconstruction is thematic overprinting, not evidence of present lakes or a modern impoundment.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern middle turn and southwestward connection
correspondence.finding: The northward turn and southwestward continuation into the broader western valley correspond to the mapped drainage. The neighboring branches remain distinct from the selected route.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower westward Magda corridor
correspondence.finding: The lower westward channel follows the mapped Magda River valley. Figures 2 and 6b connect this named corridor to the previously traced middle route.

correspondence.component_scope: Final western bends and Jungersen Bay terminal
correspondence.finding: The final bends reach Jungersen Bay’s eastern shore, north of the separately depicted Jungersen River outlet. The prose also identifies Magda River as draining into Jungersen Bay.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen Lightwood Knot Creek opening and upper tributary corridor
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening lies on the mapped Lightwood Knot Creek corridor near Sassers Mill Road, rather than at an independently determined natural river source. Repeated direct labels and a continuously depicted channel support the southward selection through the Parker Creek, Pippen Creek, Blaze Branch, Jolly Creek and Mill Creek joining settings. The mapped stream continues through the wooded wetland valley to the northern impoundment approach. Nearby side ponds are not selected through-links.

correspondence.component_scope: Impounded Lightwood Knot Creek reach near Opp and downstream outlet
correspondence.finding: The original map shows Lightwood Knot Creek entering the northern end of an elongated impoundment northwest of Opp, continuing through its waterbody, and leaving at the southwestern end into the separately drawn downstream channel. The selected route follows this same inlet, waterbody and outlet corridor. Pond Creek and Cameron Creek join the impoundment setting; Poley Creek joins downstream. The map directly labels Lightwood Knot Creek across the waterbody but does not supply a separately verified reservoir name in this inspected view. No present operating condition or regulated discharge is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Lightwood Knot Creek to Yellow River junction near Horn Hill
correspondence.finding: The Lightwood Knot Creek channel continues southwest across the highway west of Opp and meets the separately labelled Yellow River northwest of Horn Hill. The selected route uses the Lightwood approach and then continues downstream in the joined Yellow River valley. Direct cartography establishes the junction; the distinct Lightwood Knot Creek name is retained rather than replaced with Yellow River. Taylors Mill Creek and the Indian Creek system appear as additional mapped tributaries downstream.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Yellow River and Conecuh National Forest bends
correspondence.finding: Repeated Yellow River labels and the connected mapped channel support the southward valley, the westward bend through the Conecuh National Forest setting, and the further southwestward river. Indian Creek, Prices Creek, Poplar Creek, Clear Creek and North Creek are separately depicted joining streams. The generalized selection clips some meanders but remains in the same established river corridor, without a required interbasin or upland transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Alabama Yellow River and state-line crossing
correspondence.finding: The map establishes the Yellow River continuation through the lower forested Alabama valley and across the Alabama–Florida boundary. The selected parts correspond to the same continuously depicted river past Larkin Creek, Moores Mill Creek, Big Creek and Mill Creek joining settings. Surrounding ponds and the separate eastern Florala–Lake Jackson landscape are not part of the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Florida valley through Oak Grove and the Crestview approach
correspondence.finding: The original cartography repeatedly names Yellow River through Oak Grove, the Big Horse Creek join, Clear Springs, the wooded central valley, Griffin Ferry Stretch and Milligan west of Crestview. The mapped channel and wetland corridor continue through the Silver Creek, Gully Branch, Mathison Creek, Mill Creek and Trammel Creek joining settings and the highway crossings. Model lines locally simplify large bends within this connected valley; no missing through-link is supplied merely from nearby names.

correspondence.component_scope: Yellow–Shoal junction and southwestward turn
correspondence.finding: Both overlapping originals show the Yellow River descending south of the interstate and meeting the Shoal River from the east near Rattlesnake Bluff. The selected route approaches along Yellow River and turns southwest then west along the mapped joined river, which is directly labelled Yellow River below the junction. Shoal River is retained as the joining tributary name and is not assigned to the selected upstream branch.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Yellow River, side channels and Parkerville corridor
correspondence.finding: Original pixels establish the westward and southwestward lower Yellow River corridor, with repeated river labels, wooded floodplain and linked side channels through the county-boundary and Parkerville settings. Pitts River is separately labelled as a side channel in the lower network; Grimes Lake and other adjacent water features are not treated as independent long lake crossings. The selected line generalizes meanders within the same lower-river floodplain. The map supplies a connected river corridor rather than only basin membership.

correspondence.component_scope: Broxson delta connections and actual Blackwater Bay terminal
correspondence.finding: The mapped Yellow River continues through the lower wetland network past Broxson and splits into connected delta channels. The original depicts the links among the named Yellow River, Dead River and southern delta channels, with Cat Island Lake, Goggle Eye Lake, Skim Lake and Weaver River labels distinguishing local features. The selected final parts occupy this connected southern delta corridor and terminate at Blackwater Bay beside the mapped Skim Lake–Weaver River outlet setting. This establishes the actual selected terminal at ordinary delta scale; it does not assign an exact distributary or formal name-boundary vertex to each coarse modeled line, substitute a different main-river mouth, or claim present tidal flow. The bay is directly labelled in the inspected original.
